description: Open the line id+n of the view into the two lines of n/2 under it; n = 1 gives the message whole. With a subagent's id (a1) as id, it gives that subagent's whole chat; a long chat comes in pages from character at, saying where to go on.
name: zoom

description: The date and time of message id.
name: date

description: Ask Chief to sign you in when a page needs a password, passkey, 2FA code or security key, or an OAuth sign-in you cannot pass. Chief opens the page in Home's right pane, fills what it may, starts the passkey or security-key step so macOS shows Touch ID, and asks the user to touch the sensor; it tells you when the site is signed in. Never wait on a login tab and never read or type a password or code. Call it once per site.

kind.description: password, passkey, 2fa (a code or security key after the password) or oauth (a Sign in with ... page).

reason.description: One line: what you need the sign-in for.

site.description: The site's host name, for example npmjs.com.

url.description: The http(s) page where the sign-in starts.

name: escalate_auth

description: List the other subagents of Chief: id, title, state and workspace. Tell one with `tell`.
name: peers

description: Send a message to another subagent (an id from `peers`); it reads it between its tool calls (or after its current turn: a peer never interrupts it), and the message says it is from you. For Chief, write it in your report instead.

key.description: Optional idempotency key: a repeat with the same key is not sent again.

name: tell

description: Which cmux and Chief you run, read-only: the cmux CLI and the app its socket reaches (version with the nightly build, channel, build sha, bundle id and path, pid), whether the CLI is the app's own, the update state (phase, ready on quit, last check), the bundled acpmux and helper stamps, macOS, and this Chief host's version and engine (each role's harness CLI and its version).
name: version

description: MCP servers, in code mode. When the person says "connect to X" (a name like linear or deepwiki, an https URL, or a command like `npx -y @scope/server`), call action add with target X yourself: no config, no restart; it works in this same turn. A server that needs a sign-in answers with a page to open for the person (your auth-escalation flow) and you wake when it is connected. Use servers without loading their schemas: action search (query) finds tools across servers; describe (server, tool) gives TypeScript declarations; run (code) runs a script where `await mcp.<server>.<tool>({...})` calls a tool (structuredContent, or text parsed as JSON when it is; errors throw), so loop, filter and join results in the script and print only what you need. call (server, tool, args) is one direct call; with task: true (and note) it runs off your turn as an MCP task and you wake once with its result (tasks, task: id with op status|wait|cancel). subscribe (server, uri or event, note) wakes you when a resource changes or the server sends that notification (events, unsubscribe: id). Also list, remove, signin, resources, read, prompts, prompt (server, name, args). Subagents use servers but only you add or remove them.

args.description: call: the tool's arguments; prompt: the prompt's.

code.description: run: TypeScript; top-level await; `return` a value or console.log; no imports.

env.description: add: environment of a local server (kept secret).

event.description: subscribe: a notification method (notifications/message, notifications/tools/list_changed) or *.

headers.description: add: HTTP headers with a key (kept secret, never shown).

id.description: task: t<N>; unsubscribe: e<N> or all.

name.description: add: the server's name (default: from the target); prompt: the prompt.

note.description: task, subscribe: what to do when you wake.

target.description: add: a known server name, an https URL, or the command that runs a local server.

task.description: call: run off the turn as a task; you wake with its result.

name: mcp
